With uniform weights the cross-scheme re-scoring is a no-op (the order cannot change), so this run does not establish the ranking is weighting-independent, only that no weighting difference exists to test.
groupEval.fairnessExplain: Some candidates carry a bounded, evidence-driven weighting — demonstrated skill is weighted higher when backed by high-trust evidence. Each candidate is re-scored under every candidate's weighting; the robust order is the average across all schemes, so a candidate strong under everyone's weights is robustly strong.

students.exampleIntro: Three illustrative students against one junior backend role. Each carries a bounded, evidence-driven weighting — the axes are the same, how much each counts is earned. The real version of this table lives in Decisions → Group evaluation.
students.caseBadgeTitle: Fed by the case-grounded phases — these ratings gate observed minting
students.scoringFootnote: Hover a rating for the verbatim evidence behind it — no quote, no score. Adéla's case-tagged constructs average 4.3 on quoted evidence — above the 4/5 minting bar, so her case-grounded interview itself minted the observed skills that narrow her band. Bára outscores her on potential but stays wide until something is observed; Cyril's fluent delivery is scored separately from the content of his reasoning (and his 2s on the case constructs mean nothing is minted).
students.scriptIntro: The thought-script the agent follows (~{min} minutes), shown in its case-designed form. The skeleton is fixed — concrete → mechanism → counterfactual → metacognitive — and the agent may improvise follow-ups, but the highlighted phases draw their questions from the role's designed case, so every candidate works the same material. Hints are injected on purpose: coachability only exists live.
students.scriptFootnote: Every rating must cite a verbatim transcript quote (no quote, no score), a short or evasive answer widens the confidence band instead of lowering the score, and reasoning content is scored separately from delivery fluency — nerves and non-native English are not weak thinking. When the case-fed constructs all rate on quoted evidence and average above bar, the interview itself mints observed-provenance skills onto the candidate's profile.
